Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: ne-groomer[bot]
Message:
fix(freshness-monitor): hermetically stub notify_via_flow_doctor by default (#743)

test_handler_per_spec_exception_does_not_sink_pass enabled
FRESHNESS_MONITOR_ENABLED=true but never re-stubbed notify_via_flow_doctor
after its importlib.reload(index), so the per-spec-exception (probe_failed)
path called the REAL Telegram notifier whenever this suite ran with live
AWS/Telegram credentials ambient — paging the live ops-health channel with
fixture data on 2026-07-11 (alpha-engine-config#2208).

Replace flow_doctor_telegram in sys.modules with a safe no-op BEFORE any
test's import/reload of index, mirroring scheduled-groom-dispatcher's
_install_stubs fleet pattern, so a test can no longer reach the real
notifier just by forgetting a monkeypatch. Apply the same hardening to
groom-liveness-probe and usage-pace-alert, whose per-test wiring was
currently safe but fragile against the same class of gap. Also add a
deterministic backstop in notify_via_flow_doctor itself: refuse to
dispatch when context["owner_repo"] is a known test-fixture namespace
(ae-test, alpha-engine-test), independent of any test-suite stubbing.

Co-authored-by: groom-bot <groom-bot@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-authored-by: Brian McMahon <brian@nousergon.ai>

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Brian McMahon
Message:
fix(daily_closes): scrub FRED api_key from error logs + retry FRED 5xx (#220)

requests.exceptions.HTTPError.str() embeds the full request URL —
including ``api_key=<credential>`` — in its message. The existing
``_fetch_fred_closes`` except-block logged that raw via
``logger.warning("FRED fetch failed for %s (%s): %s", t, sid, e)`` so
any FRED 5xx in production MorningEnrich / EOD dumped the credential
to CloudWatch.

Surfaced 2026-05-12 during the post-merge repair run for PR #219 — a
transient FRED 500 on VXVCLS during the operator step leaked the key
to the conversation transcript. The FRED key is rotated separately;
this commit closes the leak class.

Changes:
- ``_scrub_api_key(msg) -> str`` helper in ``collectors/daily_closes.py``
  masks the ``api_key=...`` querystring fragment with ``api_key=***``
- ``_fetch_fred_closes`` warn-log routes the exception through the
  scrubber
- Repair script's ``_fetch_fred_range`` already added retry+scrub in
  the cherry-pick from the live-debug session; this commit consolidates
  by importing the shared ``_scrub_api_key`` from ``daily_closes`` so
  the regex doesn't drift across files

Tests (+7, suite 792 → 799):
- ``_scrub_api_key`` masks URL-embedded keys, handles exception objects
  directly, passthroughs when no key present, terminates at ``&``
- ``_fetch_fred_closes`` warn-log scrub regression
- ``_fetch_fred_range`` retry-warn + final-error scrub regressions

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Brian McMahon
Message:
fix(groom-dispatcher): truncate run_token in alert bodies — it wedges the alert-drain (#1216)

A bare `run_token=<32 lowercase hex>` in a lane-death / lane-reclaimed
notification body matches gitleaks' stock `generic-api-key` rule: the keyword
`token` adjacent to a high-entropy 32-char value is exactly that rule's shape.
It is not a credential — it is a correlation id this Lambda mints per lane.

Where it hurts is downstream. `_notify_cycle` publishes onto the Overseer intake
bus; alert-drain reads the queue into its LLM request; the DLP egress proxy
gitleaks-scans that outbound body and returns HTTP 400. The drain agent exits
rc=1, and because nothing is deleted from the queue without a ledger record
(overseer-policy.md invariant 8) the same message is re-read by the next run.

One lane-death alert therefore wedges the entire response plane indefinitely —
and the SQS retry ladder (`maxReceiveCount: 5`) drags the queue's *other*
messages into the DLQ five receives at a time while it does.

Measured 2026-08-03, reproduced locally against the fleet's own
`gitleaks-egress.toml` at gitleaks 8.30.1:

  - 12 of 79 sampled intake messages matched `generic-api-key`
  - every one of them from `flow-doctor:scheduled-groom-dispatcher`
  - every one of them on the `run_token=` field, in `detail.body`
  - four consecutive drain runs dead (alpha-engine-config-I6191, occurrence 4)
  - truncating the body token clears the match; scanning the post-fix message
    yields zero findings

12 hex chars stays long enough to correlate a body against the dispatch ledger
by eye. The FULL token is unchanged everywhere it is machine-read — `dedup_key`,
the `context` payload, and every log line — so truncation is a rendering change
and nothing programmatic is affected.

Guard observed failing (overseer-policy.md invariant 13): restoring the full
token to the body turns `test_lane_death_body_truncates_the_run_token` red.

Does NOT clear the messages already queued — those are immutable. See
alpha-engine-config-I6294 for the structural half.
